name: What foundation or slab does a built-in Jacuzzi need?

mainEntity.name: What kind of base, slab, or structural support is required for a built-in Jacuzzi?
mainEntity.text: What kind of base, slab, or structural support is required for a built-in Jacuzzi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The foundation for a built-in Jacuzzi must support much more than the empty shell. Once filled with water and people, the load becomes substantial, so the base needs to be level, stable, and designed for long-term support. Many projects use reinforced concrete, but the exact requirement depends on whether the spa is above grade, partially recessed, or integrated into a deck or platform. Drainage matters just as much as strength because standing water under or around the spa can damage finishes and create settlement problems. In hillside or soft-soil areas around Los Angeles, the support design may need extra engineering. The builder should confirm slab thickness, reinforcement, drainage routing, access panels, and equipment pad placement before construction begins. Homeowners should never place a built-in spa on a patio that was only designed for normal foot traffic without verification. A good design protects against cracking, settlement, and future service issues.
acceptedAnswer.description: A built-in Jacuzzi needs a properly engineered base that can support the full filled weight of the spa, water, and users. Depending on the design, that may mean a reinforced concrete slab, compacted base, structural framing, or a combination of support and drainage layers.
